# Pondhawk.Logging

> A standalone .NET structured logging API by Pond Hawk Technologies on Microsoft.Extensions.Logging (method tracing, object/typed-payload logging, [Sensitive] masking) — plus a Watch Server provider (ZLogger-based, Channel batching, dynamic switch-based level control) a journald-optimized console, an Amazon CloudWatch Logs provider, and ASP.NET Core request diagnostics. Five packages, all target net8.0, no dependency on any Pondhawk package beyond the logging API and Pondhawk.Context (the ambient `IOperationContext`: correlation id, subject, tenant).

## Packages

### Pondhawk.Logging — logging API

Install: `dotnet add package Pondhawk.Logging`

**Key types (`Pondhawk.Logging` namespace):**
- `LoggingExtensions` — extensions on `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.ILogger`:
  - `EnterMethod()` → disposable method-trace scope (auto entry/exit + elapsed)
  - `Inspect(name, value)` → logs `"{Name} = {Value}"` at Debug
  - `LogObject(value)` / `LogObject(title, value)` → serialize an object to a JSON payload
  - `LogJson` / `LogSql` / `LogXml` / `LogYaml` / `LogText(title, content)` → typed payloads with syntax-highlight hints
- `[Sensitive]` — masks a property when an object is serialized
- `PayloadType`, `JsonObjectSerializer`, `LogPropertyNames` (the `Pondhawk.*` log-state property-name contract sinks read)

Loggers come from the standard `ILoggerFactory` (`CreateLogger<T>()` / `CreateLogger(Type)` / `CreateLogger(string)`), returning `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.ILogger`.

```csharp
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Pondhawk.Logging;

using var _ = logger.EnterMethod();
logger.Inspect(nameof(orderId), orderId);
logger.LogObject("order", order);
logger.LogSql("query", sqlText);
```
**No sink or transport** — a provider (e.g. Pondhawk.Logging.Watch) supplies delivery, or an app uses any Microsoft.Extensions.Logging provider.

### Pondhawk.Logging.Watch — Watch Server provider

Install: `dotnet add package Pondhawk.Logging.Watch`
```csharp
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Pondhawk.Logging.Watch;

builder.Logging.AddWatch("http://localhost:11000/MyApp");   // Watch Server controls levels via switches
```
**Key types (`Pondhawk.Logging.Watch` namespace):**
- `WatchLoggingBuilderExtensions` — `AddWatch(this ILoggingBuilder, watchUrl, configure?)`: registers a level filter driven by the switch table and a ZLogger delivery processor
- `WatchLoggerProcessor` — a ZLogger `IAsyncLogProcessor` with unbounded `Channel<T>` batching and a circuit breaker; events serialized as MemoryPack
- `SwitchSource` / `SwitchDef` / `WatchSwitchSource` — dynamic per-category level control (longest-prefix match); `WatchSwitchSource` polls a Watch Server
- `LogEvent` / `LogEventBatch` — the wire event model

### Pondhawk.Logging.Console — journald-optimized console

Install: `dotnet add package Pondhawk.Logging.Console`
```csharp
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Pondhawk.Logging.Console;

builder.Logging.AddJournaldConsole();   // Warning and above by default; AddJournaldConsole(LogLevel.Information) for a floor of its own
```
**Key types (`Pondhawk.Logging.Console` namespace):**
- `JournaldConsoleLoggingBuilderExtensions` — `AddJournaldConsole(this ILoggingBuilder[, LogLevel minimum])`: a ZLogger console whose plain-text formatter prefixes each line with the sd-daemon priority (`<N>` mapped from `LogLevel`) and category, with no timestamp and no ANSI color; exceptions render inline (single journald entry). Fixed at Warning.

### Pondhawk.Logging.CloudWatch — Amazon CloudWatch Logs provider

Install: `dotnet add package Pondhawk.Logging.CloudWatch`
```csharp
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Pondhawk.Logging.CloudWatch;

builder.Logging.AddCloudWatch("/my-app/Production", "orders");   // Information and above; stream <instance-id>/orders
```
**Key types (`Pondhawk.Logging.CloudWatch` namespace):**
- `CloudWatchLoggingBuilderExtensions` — `AddCloudWatch(this ILoggingBuilder, logGroup, service, configure?)` and an overload taking a `CloudWatchDestination`. Level is fixed: Information and above always, Debug and Trace never, not gated by Watch switches. Touches no network; cannot stop the host starting.
- `CloudWatchOptions` — `StreamName` (null = `<instance-id>/<service>` from EC2 metadata), `Credentials`, `Region`, `RetentionDays` (30), `BatchSize`, `FlushInterval`, `MaxHeldEvents` (100)
- `CloudWatchDestination` — the log group; `Rebind(logGroup)` at runtime, `Unbound()` when the group arrives later (Warning and above held until then), `Sanitize(text)`
- `CloudWatchLoggerProcessor` — a ZLogger `IAsyncLogProcessor`: one Pascal-case JSON object per event (`Level`, `Category`, `CorrelationId`, `Title`, `Context`, `Exceptions`, `Payload`); creates its stream and a missing group on the first batch; access denied turns it off, any other failure pauses it for a minute while Warning and above is held

### Pondhawk.Logging.AspNetCore — ASP.NET Core request diagnostics

Install: `dotnet add package Pondhawk.Logging.AspNetCore`
```csharp
using Pondhawk.Logging.AspNetCore;

builder.Services.AddPondhawkDiagnostics(options => options.MaskedBodyFields.Add("password"));   // optional

app.UseDiagnosticsMonitor();      // early: Begin/End with status and elapsed time; settles the correlation id
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseDiagnosticsEnrichment();   // after authentication: subject and tenant
app.UseRequestLogging();          // deep: dumps the whole request when the category is Debug-enabled
```
**Key types (`Pondhawk.Logging.AspNetCore` namespace):**
- `DiagnosticsApplicationBuilderExtensions` — `UseDiagnosticsMonitor`, `UseDiagnosticsEnrichment`, `UseRequestLogging` on `IApplicationBuilder`
- `DiagnosticsServiceCollectionExtensions` — `AddPondhawkDiagnostics(this IServiceCollection, configure?)`
- `DiagnosticsOptions` — `CorrelationHeader` (`X-Correlation-Id`), `EchoCorrelationId` (true), `Subject` (`sub` claim, then name identifier; the subject name on each event is `preferred_username`, then `client_id`, first), `Tenant`, `Skip`, `MaskedHeaders` (`Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`), `MaskedQueryParameters` (empty), `MaskedBodyFields` (empty; form fields and JSON properties at any depth), `CaptureBody` (true), `CaptureResponseBody` (false), `MaxBodyBytes` (65536), `EndLevelByOutcome` (false)
- `DiagnosticsMonitorMiddleware`, `DiagnosticsEnrichmentMiddleware`, `RequestLoggingMiddleware`

All events use the category `Pondhawk.Diagnostics.Http`, at Debug. The monitor's End line carries the exception when the request failed. The request dump is two events with JSON payloads: the request (`Method`, `Url`, `Query`, `Endpoint`, `User`, `Headers`, `Body`) and the response (`Status`, `Elapsed`, `Headers`, and `Body` only with `CaptureResponseBody`), with `BodyOmitted` / `BodyCut` / `BodyError` beside a body. It shows what was sent — a JSON body nested as JSON, a form post as an object of fields — except `Authorization`, `Cookie` and `Set-Cookie` values; other values are masked only when named in the options. A JSON body that cannot be parsed is left out while `MaskedBodyFields` names anything. An inbound correlation id must be 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` or it is replaced. A diagnostic probe token Watch Server issued, sent in `X-Diagnostics-Probe` (`Probe`, `ProbeHeader` options), logs that request at Trace whatever the switches say, request dump included; a token that fails any check is ignored and the request goes on as if none was sent, with one Warning per token. Requires the ASP.NET Core shared framework; depends on no sink.

### Pondhawk.Logging.Migration — Fabrica.Watch migration (development-only)

Install: `<PackageReference Include="Pondhawk.Logging.Migration" PrivateAssets="all" />` — a Roslyn analyzer (`netstandard2.0`) with code fixes; nothing ships with the application. Run `dotnet format analyzers <solution> --severity info --diagnostics PHLM001 PHLM002 PHLM003 PHLM004 PHLM005 PHLM006 PHLM007 PHLM008 PHLM009 PHLM011 PHLM012 PHLM013 PHLM014 PHLM015 PHLM016 PHLM020` until it changes nothing, with Fabrica.Watch still referenced, then search for `TODO(Fabrica.Watch migration)`. It rewrites level calls (positional and interpolated messages become named-hole templates; a `Func<string>` goes behind `IsEnabled`), `Is*Enabled`, method tracing (`LeaveMethod` goes, `EnterMethod` becomes a `using`), scopes, `ErrorWithContext`/`WarningWithContext`, `Inspect`, `WatchFactoryLocator`, and swaps `using Fabrica.Watch;` for `using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;` and `using Pondhawk.Logging;` once every use left in the file means the same under them. PHLM020 rewrites an event created and logged at once; PHLM010, PHLM021–024 and other events only report. Full guide: `MIGRATING-FROM-FABRICA-WATCH.md`.

## Technical details
- All five packages target `net8.0`; built on Microsoft.Extensions.Logging (the Watch, Console and CloudWatch providers use ZLogger; `Pondhawk.Logging.AspNetCore` references the ASP.NET Core shared framework)
- XML documentation ships inside the NuGet packages (100% public-API coverage; consumers get IntelliSense)
- `Pondhawk.Logging.Watch` is consumed by the pondhawk/watch-server client
- MIT licensed; extracted from the pondhawktech/tools monorepo
